title: Edge timeout fallback and per-tenant queue isolation to reduce customer-visible 5xxs
creator: Ravi Mehta
description: Several enterprise customers reported repeated 5xx errors and long tail timeouts during tenant surges. Triage shows a pattern of the edge L7 router holding streaming connections open while backend GPU runtimes enter slow-paths (KV compaction, model warmup). This triggers connection pool exhaustion and upstream timeouts which cascade into client-side retry storms. The goal of this ticket is to implement a two-part mitigation: (1) per-tenant request queue isolation and admission controls at the edge to prevent a noisy tenant from monopolizing connection and runtime resources; (2) a graceful fallback path for requests that hit runtime slow-paths (fast, lightweight model variant or queued-shed with informative 429 + Retry-After) to avoid unknown 5xx propagation.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use tenant-simulator to open 200 concurrent streaming requests that produce long-tail KV cache compactions (script: sim/tenant_surge_stream.sh)
2) Observe edge-router metrics: growth in active connections and per-backend queue length (dashboard: Hosted > Edge > Connections)
3) Observe runtime pods: high KV eviction rate and GPU kernel stalls (runtime dashboard: runtime-1.19 > KV > compactions)
4) Trigger client SDK retries with default settings to reproduce amplification and 5xx spikes
root_cause_analysis: Edge L7 router currently lacks tenant-level admission; a single tenant with many streaming sessions can saturate the connection pool and backend request slots.
Runtime slow-path events (KV cache compaction and occasional kernel fallback for long sequences) inflate per-request latency unpredictably, exposing the edge to long-lived connections.
Client SDKs retry aggressively on timeouts/5xx; in combination with no tenant isolation this produces retry amplification and amplifies resource pressure.
Observability gaps: per-tenant inflight histograms were not enabled at the edge until 2025-02-16 which slowed triage.
mitigation: Deploy edge admission shim: token-bucket per-tenant with configurable in-flight cap (default 50 streaming connections / tenant).
Add runtime fast-fail hook: if request enters slow-path > 5s predicted tail, return 429 with Retry-After or dispatch to lightweight model variant (same API semantics).
Temporarily reduce SDK default retries for hosted tenants to 2 with exponential backoff and jitter (coord with SDK team).
Create dashboard: per-tenant inflight, edge queue depth, KV compaction events; configured alerts at >75% of per-tenant cap.
implementation_notes: Edge changes in edge-router service: admission controller implemented as middleware; config flag `tenant_inflight_limit` added (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/1892).
Runtime changes: add lightweight model routing in router service (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-router/pull/854).
SDK change: short-lived patch to hosted SDK to lower default retries (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/621).
Backwards compatibility: tenant isolation is opt-out for Dedicated/Private deployments via config `edge.enable_tenant_isolation=false` to respect on-prem network topologies.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary edge admission shim in us-west-2 for low-risk tenants (1% traffic) for 2 hours; monitor connection pool and 5xx rate.
2) If stable, expand to all hosted regions over 6 hours with 10% increments.
3) Simultaneously roll runtime fast-fail to the same canary pool and ensure no observable regressions in short prompt accuracy tests.
4) Coordinate SDK patch release and email notice to customers about changed retry behavior and recommended SDK upgrade.
5) Post-rollout: enable per-tenant alerts and schedule 48-hour observation window with on-call rotation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for edge admission logic and token-bucket behavior.
Integration test harness: tenant-simulator with controlled slow-path kernel delays to validate fast-fail routes.
Chaos test: inject artificial KV compactions in staging to validate fallback to lightweight model and no 5xx escalation.
Load test: ramp to tenant-concurrent scenarios in perf lab to tune default caps (50 -> 100).
observability_and_alerting: Alerts: edge.tenant.inflight_count > 75% of limit for 5m -> P1 pager; runtime.slowpath.rate > 0.5% of requests -> investigate root cause.
customer_communication: Drafted status email for affected customers: Confluence draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ENG-333321+-+Tenant+Isolation+Draft
Support playbook: how to interpret 429+Retry-After vs 5xx and recommended SDK upgrade (doc link in support KB)
Planned customer follow-up after 72h stability window with root-cause summary and recommended config knobs for Dedicated/Private.
